text:
emma: Escalation from AcmeMobile — customer seeing JSON.parse errors when consuming streaming JSON in JSON-mode. They say the stream sometimes ends with a partial object (missing closing brace) and client throws. Attaching repro + logs below. Severity: high, customer-facing bug.

kevin: Can you paste the exact request + headers they use? streaming type (SSE vs chunked) + approximate latency when it happens?

emma: They use SSE (text/event-stream) with structured output mode (server sends JSON objects per event). Headers: `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `X-App: acme-mobile`. Happens after ~40-60s on bad requests. Customer provided truncated tail:```\ndata: {"id":"msg_42","tokens":["hello","world"],"meta":{"usage":42}  \\n```
(note: missing `}` and final `\\n

kevin: Do we have any gateway/nginx/nginx-like edge in front of our backend? Could be proxy buffer/window/timeouts closing connection mid-chunk. Also is client on HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1?

emma: Customer on iOS app, uses mobile carrier NAT + CDN edge (CloudFront in front of their proxy). Our edge is CF too. Their client shows socket FIN from remote right after last bytes. Server logs show 200 OK and ~1.1KB sent, then `write: connection reset by peer` in runtime.

maria: Check our ingress configs for `proxy_read_timeout` and `send_timeout`. If intermediary closes idle connections aggressively you'll see tail cuts. Can you paste the route id and any nginx config?

emma: Route: `redwood-prod/sse/stream-v2` (route-id: rwd-5012). Ingress snippet the customer shared from their side:```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 30s;
send_timeout 10s;
keepalive_timeout 5s;
```
They also have `http2` enabled.

sam: Repro tip: try `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?mode=json"` and kill the client after ~50s to simulate carrier close. Also try `nghttp -v` for h2 repro. I'll run an internal job to stream a 90s payload and watch chunk boundaries.

observability-bot: Trace created: https://redwood.internal/traces/trace-abc123 (shows upstream wrote final chunk at 52s then RST from client at 52s + 2ms)

kevin: Trace looks like server finished writing but client/edge closed immediately. That matches early FIN from an intermediary. Two mitigations: 1) send periodic SSE comment heartbeats (e.g., `: ping\\n\\n`) so the carrier sees activity; 2) make each event self-contained (avoid very long objects split across TCP packets) or send chunk boundary safe framing (length-prefix).

emma: Customer prefers structured-mode (JSON per event). Suggested short-term mitigations: lower per-object size (stream partial fields), add heartbeat event every 10s. Also asked if backend could detect abrupt EOF and attempt short buffer flush to rewrite a closing `}` — is that safe?

sam: Auto-fixing partial JSON on close is risky (can mask real errors). If we implement a small heuristic it must be opt-in and logged (e.g., `streaming_tolerate_partial: true`). For now recommend heartbeat + client-side tolerant parser that can handle a truncated final object as a partial result.

maria: Also check if our keepalive probes to upstream are triggering connection reuse issues (http2 stream reset). We saw similar earlier with mobile proxies that don't like long-lived h2 streams. Try forcing `Connection: keep-alive` on the client and see if that changes behavior.

emma: I'll ask customer for client socket traces and their proxy logs (they promised). I'll also spin up the internal repro with `curl -N` and `nghttp` and report results. If reproducible, we'll engage eng-runtime to discuss an opt-in tolerant mode.

kevin: Thanks — if you can reproduce, please paste minimal curl + nghttp commands and any pcap or `ss/tcpdump` evidence. If it's an ISP/proxy, we should document guidance in docs (heartbeat + smaller objects).

emma: Will do. Assigning to eng-runtime if repro confirmed. I will update ticket and loop in the customer success manager. :thumbsup:
